item.title: NPR: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
item.description: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.

item.title: NPR: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
item.description: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.

item.title: NPR: Legal scholar Stephen Vladeck on Texas' new Democratic AG and federal litigation
item.description: NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.

item.title: NPR: Trump faces bipartisan backlash over plan to sell public lands to states and tribes
item.description: The Trump administration wants to sell some federal public lands to states, local governments and tribes, a plan that's once again drawing swift bi-partisan opposition.

item.title: NPR: As Democrats win big, thirst traps of male candidates take social media by storm
item.description: It's everywhere on social media: Democrats celebrating the attractive men voters elected in the midterms. But it's bigger than a meme and says a lot about politics of masculinity in the age of Trump.

item.title: NPR: Hegseth's failed impeachment was a warning to Democrats. Where will they go from here?
item.description: Democrats have been given a huge opportunity with majorities in both the House and Senate — but the balance of priorities, timing, messaging and discipline are all going to be major tests.

item.title: NPR: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
item.description: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt
item.description: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster malfunctioned and ended up in the water Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'
item.description: Air travel across the country came to a standstill on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop citing "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety." Aviation correspondent Miles O'Brien reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Tanker crashes into river cruise boat in New Orleans
item.description: In our news wrap Friday, a ship collided with a river cruise boat in New Orleans, causing it to sink in the Mississippi River, some Microsoft users were offline for a second day as the company scrambled to restore its widely used suite of workplace software and the White House is tightening rules on how staffers interact with lobbyists.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bessent accuses Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia chips
item.description: The fallout of Jensen Huang's downfall expanded into a public fight between two of President Trump's top advisers. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia's most advanced chips. Nick Schifrin looks at the finger-pointing and the ongoing efforts to control advanced technology exports to China.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Increasing cost of housing squeezes Americans out of market
item.description: Sales of existing homes in the U.S. fell last month to their lowest level in more than 16 years. That's according to a new report by the National Association of Realtors. In October alone, sales dropped to 3.75 million homes, an 8.8% drop compared with the same time last year. Stephanie Sy reports on what's driving the decline.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Does Van Hollen have enough support to beat Schumer in Senate leadership race?
item.description: Senate Democrats won back their majority last week, and now they're fighting over who will lead it. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen has thrown his hat in the ring and says he will take on current Democratic leader Chuck Schumer. Congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins reports on the first serious challenge Schumer has faced to his party leadership.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: ICE touts record number of deportations in agency's history
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security reports that immigrant deportations and arrests hit an all-time high. More than 491,000 people were arrested by ICE in the last fiscal year, and more than 483,000 were deported. The Trump administration has said it aims to deport one million immigrants annually. William Brangham discussed more with John Sandweg, who was acting ICE Director under President Obama.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about Microsoft's outage and why it takes so long to restore email services
item.description: Unlike modern web apps or authentication gatekeepers, email wasn't designed to fail fast, meaning to immediately halt when a problem arises.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooks and Marcus on how Republicans are responding to midterm losses
item.description: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Ruth Marcus of The New Yorker join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the fallout of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and what the Trump administration knew, how Republicans are responding to their losses in the midterm elections, JD Vance's chances in 2028 and the Democratic leadership battle in the Senate.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Celebrated countertenor brings classical sound to today's cultural issues
item.description: Anthony Roth Costanzo cuts an unusual figure in the world of music. The leading international opera singer is performing in the Metropolitan Opera's critically acclaimed and wildly popular "Lincoln at the Bardo," which the Met will stream for free to the public on Saturday. Senior arts correspondent Jeffrey Brown has the story for our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: NPR: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Homeland Security Secretary Mullin says FAA flight stoppage 'isn't another 9/11'
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there are no indications of an attack against the nation, after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon due to communications problems.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. wrongly withheld New York highway funds over immigrant licenses, appeals court rules
item.description: The U.S. Transportation Department wrongly decided to withhold nearly $74 million in highway money from New York state after it refused to revoke nearly 33,000 questionable commercial driver's licenses for immigrants when an audit revealed problems last year, a federal appeals court said Friday.

item.title: NPR: DHS head Mark Waye Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mark Waye Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

item.title: NPR: The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?
item.description: Federal judge Ana Reyes grilled the government on Friday about its plans for East Potomac Park, and indicated she could order it to remain open despite President Trump's renovation wishes.

item.title: NPR: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
item.description: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: FAA grounds all flights at U.S. airports due to air traffic control communications problems
item.description: The FAA notice said the ground stop was being imposed "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: GOP Rep. Lauren Boebert of Colorado loses U.S. House seat to Democrat Eileen Laubacher
item.description: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated Rep. Lauren Boebert for a Colorado U.S. House seat on Friday, ousting a three-term Republican and staple of conservative media.

item.title: NPR: Latino voters help fuel Kansas' blue wave
item.description: In southwest Kansas, three majority-Latino counties shocked the political establishment by going blue for the first time in decades. Voters and activists say immigration enforcement was a big factor.

item.title: NPR: DEM SENATE LEADER FIGHT
item.description: Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change, but as the party gets ready to retake the majority in both the House and Senate, there are divides over who should lead it.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Rescues operations underway in New Orleans after tanker hits river cruise boat
item.description: A tanker struck a New Orleans river cruise with 129 passengers on board on Friday, partially submerging the boat. Rescues were underway on the Mississippi River, officials say.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Brooklyn community leaders, residents hold meeting on building collapse
item.description: New York officials, from building inspectors to prosecutors, say they're investigating what caused the three-story building to come crashing down as workers were digging at an adjacent construction site. Those who lost family, neighbors and their homes demanded answers.

item.title: NPR: Rachel Maddow says the Justice Department is collapsing. Can it be saved?
item.description: Was the Justice Department ever really above politics? Rachel Maddow digs into its surprising past to explain why she believes its future is at stake.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: UN chief says 'immediate and drastic' emissions cuts needed to avert climate change catastrophe
item.description: "You cannot build peace on a burning planet," United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres told reporters, stressing that climate change is central to the U.N.'s work because it contributes to geopolitical instability.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court will consider Trump's executive order suspending asylum access at the southern border
item.description: The Trump administration wants to overturn lower court decisions that found the executive order banning asylum applications is illegal. Federal law gives people the right to seek asylum if they fear persecution in their home countries, no matter how they arrived in the U.S.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: UK police launch sex offense investigation into children's author and TV personality David Walliams
item.description: The Metropolitan Police said it had received a number of allegations of past abuse following the joint investigation this week by ITV News and the Guardian newspaper.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'TrumpCare' and commemorative plaques — how Democrats are pitching deal-making with the president
item.description: Democrats who swept into power by riding voter backlash to Trump are now pitching ways to collaborate with the president, playing to his vanity and his love of making deals to propel their own agenda.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Europe to send a diplomat team to Ukraine talks as leaders push for a voice
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa said the continent will be represented by the EU and five members of the "coalition of the willing" that backs Ukraine: the U.K., France, Germany, Italy and Poland.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What men need to know after a major update to prostate cancer guidelines
item.description: Middle-aged men should undergo regular screening for prostate cancer, the American Cancer Society said Thursday in a major change to its guidelines.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Meet the new 'Bachelor,' a quarterback for the Washington Commanders
item.description: After a troubled year for "The Bachelor" franchise, the ABC reality dating show is going back to a familiar well: the NFL. The network announced Friday that Sam Hartman, a quarterback for the Washington Commanders, will be handing out roses on the 30th season of the show.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bigger and more-frequent wildfires threaten water supplies across the U.S.
item.description: Wildfires leave behind charred trees and scorched vegetation that impact the streams and rivers providing drinking water to much of the country, and new studies show that contamination could remain for more than a decade.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bessent blames Lutnick's Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chips to China
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has come under increasing scrutiny because of his reportedly close relationship with Jensen Huang.

item.title: NPR: The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
item.description: Election officials are preparing for the Trump administration's pressure tactics over potential noncitizens on state voter rolls to continue, though recent court rulings pose new obstacles.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Navy has quietly fired some commanders and other officials, drawing congressional pushback
item.description: The firings are a break from the Navy's longstanding policy to announce major removals of commanders and other highly visible officials. They also follow an increasing level of secrecy over military operations, especially in the Middle East.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats are weighing impeachment of RFK Jr. while courting his supporters
item.description: When Democrats take over Congress in January, one of their many oversight targets will be Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., whose overhaul of longstanding vaccine guidance and cuts to medical research over the past two years have drawn fiery criticism. Some high-ranking lawmakers have suggested impeaching him.
item.category: Secretary of Health and Human Services

item.title: PBS NewsHour: High airfares may become new norm as jet fuel costs soar, says Asia-Pacific airline industry chief
item.description: High airfares could become the new norm as airlines contend with soaring jet fuel prices and mounting operating costs, the Association of Asia Pacific Airlines' chief said Friday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump's Justice Department faces a new era of scrutiny under a Democratic-led Congress
item.description: The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress as it pursued investigations into President Donald Trump's enemies, fired waves of career employees and defended administration stances that judges across the country repeatedly deemed legally dubious.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ukraine fires nearly 1,200 drones at Russia as U.S.-led talks consider wider European security
item.description: Ukraine fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow's invasion nearly five years ago.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
item.description: Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party swept to power in the midterm elections.

item.title: NPR: Nvidia CEO steps down. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen to run for majority leader
item.description: Nvidia's chief financial officer has been appointed interim CEO after Jensen Huang stepped down from the role. And, Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for majority leader.

item.title: NPR: Hegseth awards medal to soldier who chastised him
item.description: Pete Hegseth was yelled at by a sentinel for poor decorum at Arlington National Cemetery. Now the Secretary of Defense has given him a medal.

item.title: NPR: These swing voters have low expectations for divided government
item.description: Key voters in North Carolina are pessimistic the blue wave flipping control of Congress will solve their economic woes. Many say President Trump will be the chief obstacle.

item.title: NPR: These two voter turnout trends explain what happened across the South in the election
item.description: In six states across the Deep South, a drastic swing to the left this election was driven by high Black voter turnout and compounded by a sharp decline in voting rates across Republican-heavy areas.

item.title: NPR: Trump redirects Vance from Iran to focus on combatting fraud in Democratic-led states
item.description: President Trump now says there is no need for an Iran deal, pushing Vice President Vance to instead focus on battling corruption.

item.title: NPR: These swing voters have low expectations for divided government
item.description: Key voters in North Carolina are pessimistic the blue wave flipping control of Congress will solve their economic woes. Many say President Trump will be the chief obstacle.

item.title: NPR: Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader
item.description: Van Hollen, a progressive from Maryland, said voters sent a clear message in the midterm elections — that they want "change from the status quo."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Senators probe RFK Jr.'s reason for Samoa trip after letter refuting his testimony published
item.description: Two Democratic senators are launching an investigation into whether Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. lied to Congress about his reason for a 2019 trip to Samoa after The Associated Press and The Guardian published documents in August refuting his testimony.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about dengue fever as Florida reports more than 500 cases this year
item.description: As Florida navigates its largest dengue outbreak in more than 15 years, it might help to understand how this virus spreads and how to recognize symptoms and protect yourself.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: In Somalia, USAID cuts have life-or-death consequences
item.description: Since the Trump administration began its reductions to foreign aid, we've brought you reports from around the world on the consequences. Wracked by conflict for decades and suffering the cruel effects of the climate crisis, Somalia is perpetually in need. In partnership with the Pulitzer Center, Neha Wadekar and Ed Ram show how the cuts are affecting some of the world's most vulnerable people.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A Brief But Spectacular take on finding purpose after military service
item.description: After 24 years in the Army, Quinton McNair returned home to Chicago and found himself struggling to adjust to civilian life. But an unexpected hobby helped him discover a new sense of mission. He shares his Brief But Spectacular take on finding purpose after the military.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What Huang's resignation mean for chipmakers, AI and U.S. national security
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation after it was reported that he had an affair with a businesswoman accused of being a Chinese spy and an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive. Huang's departure has sparked questions about the future of Nvidia, the AI industry and U.S. national security. Amna Nawaz discussed the latest with Dmitri Alperovitch and Stephen Witt.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New York building collapse kills 8, including 2 children
item.description: New York officials say they've ended their rescue operations at the site of a collapsed building in Brooklyn and that there are no more victims inside. The collapse killed at least eight people, including two children, and injured dozens more. William Brangham reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: 1 killed and 4 injured in D.C. shooting
item.description: In our news wrap Thursday, a gunman in Washington, D.C., killed one person and injured 4 others before fatally shooting himself, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded a medal today to the soldier who admonished his party during a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery and European officials will join the next round of Ukraine peace talks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How Scott Colom won his longshot bid to flip Mississippi's Senate seat
item.description: In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom won his longshot bid to oust incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. Colom's victory is a stunning reversal in the deeply conservative state that hasn't been represented by a Black senator since the Reconstruction era following the Civil War. Liz Landers reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Scott Colom's historic victory marks 'new moment' for Black voters, Bryan Stevenson says
item.description: Scott Colom's historic victory in Mississippi marks a political milestone in a state central to the struggle for civil rights and voting rights in America. To discuss the significance of this moment, Geoff Bennett spoke with Bryan Stevenson, founder and executive director of the Equal Justice Initiative.

item.title: NPR: Cindy Holscher wins in Kansas, holding governor's office for Democrats
item.description: Holscher, a state senator, overcame a more well-known Republican who had Trump's endorsement in the state that has gone to the GOP in most other statewide races.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Abdul El-Sayed on Democratic leadership, health care access and inspiring a new generation
item.description: The new wave of Democratic senators are in Washington for orientation and are already facing tough questions about how they plan to govern. One is Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, the first Muslim elected to the Senate. His win came after a hard-fought race marked by outside spending and attacks on his name and his faith. Amna Nawaz sat down with El-Sayed to discuss how he hopes to shake up Washington.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Cindy Holscher wins election for Kansas governor, extending Democrats' wave of victories
item.description: Holscher, a state senator, promised to halt new data centers and overcame a flood of money that Republicans poured behind Ty Masterson, the president of the GOP-controlled state Senate.

item.title: NPR: Cindy Holscher wins in Kansas, holding governor's office for Democrats
item.description: Holscher, a state senator, overcame a more well-known Republican who had Trump's endorsement in the state that has gone to the GOP in most other statewide races.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What we know after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO
item.description: Nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Thursday, effective immediately. The California-based company said that Colette Kress — who has been Nvidia's chief financial officer and executive vice president since 2013 — will step into the role of interim CEO.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sen. Blumenthal says federal prosecutor attempting to investigate him for conducting an inquiry
item.description: Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, who is set to chair the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations when the Democratic majority takes control of the Senate next year, said the implied investigation is baseless.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: 'More questions than answers' about Nvidia's Huang, Jeffries says in news conference
item.description: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries is demanding a classified briefing for all members of Congress about the Nvidia situation.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: After emotional return, Pope Leo denounces 'machismo' in Peru and demands respect for women
item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Thursday denounced widespread "machismo" and violence against women in Peru, demanding that women be protected and respected as he set out marching orders for his beloved Peruvian church and people.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump administration officials announce PTSD research funding for psychedelic drug ibogaine
item.description: Federal officials on Thursday announced new funding to explore the medical potential of ibogaine, a controversial psychedelic drug championed by veterans, conservative lawmakers and podcasters aligned with President Donald Trump.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats gather in Denver for post-midterms introspection-turned-celebration
item.description: The two-day What's Next conference, hosted by a new group called Majority Democrats, was put on politicos' calendars months ago as another stepping stone as the party charted its way out of its post-2024 political wilderness.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Alaska judge rules a request by Peltola campaign for ballot data in Senate race is 'not reasonable'
item.description: An Alaska judge ruled Wednesday that a request by Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign for a list of absentee voters whose ballots have been rejected is "not reasonable," particularly given the time crunch election officials face as they continue counting ballots from last week's election.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump administration plans to make it harder to get grocery assistance
item.description: About 6.3 million people could lose eligibility for SNAP by the 2029 fiscal year if the proposed change takes effect, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. That is on top of 5.5 million people who already have lost SNAP benefits over the past year.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hegseth presents award to soldier who scolded him and his aides at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
item.description: The scolding drew attention once more to the embattled defense secretary, who had survived an impeachment attempt the day before.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: House approves bill to boost compensation for many veterans, with some floor drama
item.description: The centerpiece of the package is an effort to boost compensation for an estimated 58,000 veterans who are medically retired because of combat-related injuries. That objective has broad, bipartisan support in Congress, but lawmakers and veterans groups aren't on the same page about how to get there.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. envoys meet with Putin in Moscow on Ukraine talks, then head for Dublin to see Zelenskyy
item.description: Kushner and Witkoff met with Putin in a meeting that lasted about two hours. They then headed for Dublin for talks with Zelenskyy as the conflict stretches toward the five-year mark.

item.title: NPR: Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
item.description: As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooklyn building collapse death toll rises to 8 as rescuers search for survivors
item.description: Search crews peered into crevices in the rubble, pulling out victims and at least one survivor through the overnight hours. The cause was still under investigation.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Suspected gunman shoots 5 people in D.C., killing 1, before dying by suicide
item.description: Jeffery Carroll, interim chief with the Metropolitan Police Department, said that the man apparently had a dispute with the building's homeowners association.

item.title: NPR: DC shooting leaves 1 person killed, 4 injured. Gunman dead
item.description: A gunman opened fire at a gym in Washington, D.C.'s Logan Circle Thursday morning. One person has been confirmed killed and four others injured. The gunman is dead, according to police.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sharp swings for Nvidia and oil prices weigh on Wall Street
item.description: Nvidia's stock plunged as much as 14% at the start of trading following the resignation of Jensen Huang, its CEO, co-founder and face of the brand.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises national security concerns
item.description: Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday, media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him.

item.title: NPR: White House warns Trump probes could be criminal. Rep. Robert Garcia won't back down
item.description: Incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman Robert Garcia says Democrats won't be intimidated by White House threats over their planned investigations: "It's in the Constitution."

item.title: NPR: Colom wins Mississippi Senate race. And, White House warns Dems over future probes
item.description: After more than a week of counting ballots, Scott Colom has narrowly won the Mississippi Senate seat. And, the White House has sent a letter warning Democrats who plan to investigate the administration.

item.title: NPR: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
item.description: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

item.title: NPR: A blue wave helped offset for now a falling tally of Black members in the U.S. House
item.description: A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now.

item.title: NPR: How Scott Colom defied the odds to go from district attorney to Mississippi's Democratic US Senator
item.description: In a state that hasn't had a Democrat in office since 1980 and hasn't sent a Black Senator to Washington since the 1870s, Colom's win represents a massive upset in state politics.

item.title: NPR: Senators don't always share bill text online before votes. They should, advocates say
item.description: The text of what lawmakers are considering isn't always made available for public review before it is voted on. A group of open governance advocates is calling on Senate leadership for a change.

item.title: NPR: Rep. Bennie Thompson discusses the U.S. Senate race Democrat win in Mississippi
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson, of Mississippi, about Democrat Scott Colom's U.S. Senate victory.

item.title: NPR: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi. After a very close race, he's the first Black man to represent the state in the Senate in nearly 150 years.

item.title: NPR: Michigan Senator-elect El Sayed discusses Democrats' ambitions
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) about his win in the midterms and what's at the top of his agenda once he begins his first term in Congress.

item.title: NPR: Incoming House Oversight Committee chair Robert Garcia reacts to White House warning
item.description: NPR's A Martinez asks Democratic Rep. Robert Garcia of California about 2027 House Oversight plans to investigate the Trump administration and the response from White House to his plans.

item.title: NPR: White House warns Democrats over future probes, citing possible 'criminality'
item.description: The White House has taken an aggressive posture at the prospect of new Democratic oversight, when the new Congress comes in, next year.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Indictment sheds light on alleged Iran-backed plots across U.S. and Europe
item.description: Iran's top national security official warned that it would strike American bases beyond the Gulf, including in Europe, if the United States resumes air strikes against the Islamic Republic. The warning comes one day after indictments in New York against three men who allegedly conspired to attack U.S. Air Force planes at a base in England. Nick Schifrin reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Democrat Scott Colom defeats Mississippi Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith
item.description: In our news wrap Wednesday, Democrat Scott Colom has defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, a group that included Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was admonished by an Army sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the U.S. ended with an agreement to exchange prisoners, but no breakthrough on ending the war.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How companies are using AI to make you spend more money
item.description: Companies have always tried to maximize profits, but now there are a host of sophisticated tools to determine the prices of the goods and services they sell. At a time when so many Americans are frustrated with rising costs, those tools are under greater scrutiny. Economics correspondent Paul Solman explains how that technology is transforming the prices we pay.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How America's military shaped the nation's history and evolved over 250 years
item.description: Over the last 250 years, the United States military has helped shape the nation's history – from the fight for independence to its emergence as the world's leading military power. But as the military's reach has grown, fewer Americans are serving in uniform. Judy Woodruff explores what that means for the country in her series, Crossroads: America at 250.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New film 'The Mosquito Bowl' tells story of WWII football game between Marines
item.description: The themes of service to country and reflection on humanity are at the center of the new film "The Mosquito Bowl." Special correspondent Mike Cerre caught up with some of the forces behind the film and the real historical event. It's part of our arts and culture series, CANVAS.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 2026 Midterm Election results
PBS NewsHour: White House threatens Democrats over plans to investigate Trump officials
item.description: With Democrats set to take control of Congress, the White House is threatening them over investigations into the Trump administration. The top White House lawyer warned that aggressive oversight of the administration "may cross the line into blatant criminality." It comes amid a wave of resignations within the Justice Department. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Devlin Barrett of The New York Times.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sen. Coons on Huang affair, Iran war and why Trump should fire Hegseth
item.description: As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress, Delaware Sen. Chris Coons is poised to become chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, succeeding retiring Democrat Jeanne Shaheen. A staunch supporter of Ukraine and a critic of President Trump's war with Iran, Coons would take the helm at a consequential moment for American foreign policy. Coons joined Geoff Bennett to discuss more.

item.title: NPR: Democrat Scott Colom wins the closest Senate race in the country
item.description: Mississippi hadn't elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate in more than 40 years.

item.title: NPR: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom has won election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi, according to a race call by the Associated Press, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Scott Colom wins Senate election in Mississippi
item.description: Democratic nominee Scott Colom has defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's closely contested U.S. Senate race after a prolonged ballot counting process, giving the state its first Black U.S. senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Russia and Ukraine agree to a large prisoner exchange as talks end with no major breakthrough
item.description: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war, both sides said Wednesday as two days of U.S.-mediated talks concluded with no major breakthrough on ending Moscow's nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 4 key findings in the Jeffrey Epstein report from GOP-led House Oversight panel
item.description: Jeffrey Epstein's crimes committed after 2005 could have been prevented, barring "repeated failures" from law enforcement and federal prosecutors. That's one of the findings in a report published Tuesday by the House Oversight Committee after an investigation into the late convicted sex offender and his associates.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Biden says he wouldn't have run for a second term in 2024 if he knew he had cancer
item.description: Joe Biden says he did not know he had cancer while he was president and would not have sought a second term if he already had been diagnosed.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge allows Trump defamation case against BBC to proceed but tosses 1 claim
item.description: President Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation case against the BBC remains on track, for the moment.

item.title: NPR: Who is Jim Jordan, the House Republicans' pick for minority leader?
item.description: As House Republicans prepare for life in the minority, they're turning to Jim Jordan as their next leader. In Jordan, they've picked a conservative firebrand and one of Trump's most vocal defenders.

item.title: NPR: These voters are looking for change, but don't have high hopes for a divided Congress
item.description: North Carolina swing voters are seeking change, but have low expectations that things will actually change.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump says the towering arch he wants to be build might be dedicated to military veterans
item.description: President Donald Trump observed Veterans Day by suggesting that the towering arch he wants to build in his own honor would also be dedicated to the U.S. military and those who served in its ranks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Missing South Carolina infant rescued after being buried alive in a dog crate for 24 hours
item.description: When an 11-month-old infant was reported missing in South Carolina, dozens of first responders combed the countryside for the "bright boy with reddish blond hair" who, the sheriff's office said, had disappeared while his grandmother ran errands.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: More than a dozen key races remain too early to call one week after Election Day
item.description: The size of Democrats' majorities in the House and Senate remained undetermined one week after Election Day as more than a dozen races were still too early to call Tuesday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington
item.description: Extramarital affairs are usually private matters. Jensen Huang's has global implications.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP report: Bessent moves to a military base over safety concerns
item.description: Recent U.S. intelligence showed that Iran has stepped up efforts to target American personnel in the Middle East and elsewhere.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Read the letter the White House's top lawyer sent Rep. Garcia over threats to investigate Trump
item.description: The White House's top lawyer sent a letter of warning to incoming House Oversight Committee chair Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., on Wednesday, claiming that the Democrats' promise to investigate the Trump administration "may cross the line into blatant criminality."
item.category: House Oversight and Government Reform Committee

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: SS United States, once world's fastest ocean liner, sinks to become reef off Florida
item.description: The historic ocean liner SS United States will be intentionally sunk Wednesday off the coast of the Florida panhandle.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: White House sends warning to Democrats about investigating the Trump administration
item.description: The White House has issued a warning to Democrats over their planned probes into the Trump administration, going as far as claiming that such investigations — a standard oversight function of Congress -- may amount to "blatant criminality."

item.title: NPR: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: NPR: What's behind Democratic Socialists' historic victories in the midterms?
item.description: Historian and The New Yorker writer Jill Lepore says the DSA, once maligned, is no longer "beyond the political pale." She discusses the history of socialism in America, and its current resurgence.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge weighs lawsuit brought by Peltola campaign over absentee ballots in Alaska's Senate race
item.description: The campaign of Alaska Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola is seeking a list of absentee voters whose ballots have been rejected in one of the most closely watched races of the midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump marks Veterans Day with wreath laying, remarks at Arlington National Cemetery
item.description: On Tuesday, nine family members of the Kennedy political dynasty asked a judge to block President Donald Trump's plan to build a towering memorial arch, saying the 250-foot structure would cast a shadow over their relatives' gravesites at Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: NPR: Following big Democratic wins, these swing voters are looking for results
item.description: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.

item.title: NPR: House effectively ends Hegseth impeachment. And, 3 men accused of plotting U.K. attacks
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been spared from the House's impeachment effort, at least for now. And, federal prosecutors arrested three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives.

item.title: NPR: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch
item.description: Descendants of President John F. Kennedy are asking a judge to block President Trump's monumental arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: NPR: Republican advisor about discusses the GOP's leadership vote
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and advisor to House Speaker Mike Johnson, about the new GOP's leadership vote.

item.title: NPR: Iran-backed trio accused of plotting attacks on U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
item.description: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

item.title: NPR: Kennedys sue to block Trump's arch, citing shadow over JFK's grave
item.description: Descendants of President John F. Kennedy are asking a judge to block President Trump's monumental arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: NPR: Ex-CIA officer on UK investigations into alleged Iran, Russia threats
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with former CIA senior executive clandestine service officer Daniel Hoffman about investigations in Britain into alleged threats linked to Iran and Russia.

item.title: NPR: Close Trump ally to lead House Republicans next year
item.description: House Republicans will have a new leader at the start of the new Congress in January: Ohio's Jim Jordan, a co-founder of the ultra-conservative Freedom Caucus and a close ally of President Trump.

item.title: NPR: House votes to end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth
item.description: The House was on course for a floor vote Wednesday on whether to impeach Pete Hegseth. That is until House Republicans used a procedural vote to effectively end the impeachment effort.

item.title: NPR: Mixed results from ballot measures on abortion and trans issues
item.description: Midterm ballot measures on abortion and transgender issues saw mixed results.

item.title: NPR: Steve Inskeep talks to ex-CIA analyst about alleged Nvidia Chinese spy case
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep talks with former CIA analyst Emily Harding about China's spy tactics in light of the alleged plot targeting the CEO of Nvidia.

item.title: NPR: Michel Martin speaks to Republican advisor about GOP leadership vote
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and advisor to House Speaker Mike Johnson, about the new GOP's leadership vote.

item.title: NPR: Ex-GOP lawmaker, turned California Independent, talks reelection bid defeat
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Rep. Kevin Kiley (I-Calif.) who officially left the GOP in March and lost his bid for reelection last week.

item.title: NPR: AI hoaxes are deceiving 911 dispatchers, and they're only getting harder to detect
item.description: Swatters are increasingly using AI technology that creates synthetic voices or sound effects to generate remarkably believable fake emergency calls to law enforcement.

item.title: NPR: Both sides now? Critics slam DOJ moves to dismiss convictions of Trump allies
item.description: The DOJ moved to dismiss criminal convictions of former Trump adviser Steve Bannon and of the Oath Keepers, in what it calls "the interests of justice." Critics are crying foul.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: House rejects Hegseth impeachment as GOP selects Jordan and Thune as leaders
item.description: Power shifts in Washington continued as new party leadership began to take shape. In the House, the GOP picked Jim Jordan to be their new leader and Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune. The House also voted to quash an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Lisa Desjardins reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A breakdown of the impeachment articles filed against Pete Hegseth
item.description: For a legal perspective on the effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Geoff Bennett spoke with Eugene Fidell. He's a longtime military law expert who served as a Coast Guard lawyer and later practiced military law in the private sector. He also co-founded the National Institute of Military Justice, an organization dedicated to improving the military justice system.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Mississippi voters reflect on surprising Senate race as count continues
item.description: Mississippi, a state not known for close elections, now sits in the center of the national spotlight as an unusually high number of absentee and provisional ballots will determine the size of the Democratic majority in the Senate. In partnership with the Pulitzer Center, Liz Landers reports on how election officials are handling the ongoing vote count and the historic nature of this Senate race.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. inflation report highlights strain of rising food, energy and housing costs
item.description: High inflation persisted last month, providing little relief for Americans struggling with affordability. It is driven largely by food and energy price increases, but housing costs also rose. The country appears to be headed for an annual inflation rate of about 4% this year. To discuss what it means for the economy, Geoff Bennett spoke with Austan Goolsbee of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.

item.title: NPR: Supreme Court seems split over federal agencies' ability to fine for law violations
item.description: The Supreme Court heard arguments Tuesday in a case related to temporary worker visas. The company involved says enforcement issues should go through the courts, not the federal agency alone.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'A Matter of Hope' shines light on social entrepreneurs tackling big issues
item.description: Jim Bildner is the CEO of the Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation, one of the world's largest venture philanthropy organizations. It finds and funds entrepreneurs tackling big issues from health care access to clean water initiatives. In his new book, "A Matter of Hope," Bildner shares stories of impact and how hope fuels that work. He sat down with Amna Nawaz to discuss more.

item.title: NPR: House GOP faults the federal government for failing to hold Epstein accountable
item.description: The House Oversight Committee has released a report into its investigation into sex-offender, Jeffrey Epstein. They faulted the federal government for not holding the financier accountable.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: U.S. charges 3 with plotting attacks at air base and Jewish communities
item.description: In our news wrap Wednesday, the U.S. charged three men with being Iran-backed operatives who planned to carry out attacks on Jewish communities and plotting an attack at a British airbase, Russian and Ukrainian representatives met for peace talks for the first time in nine months and Israel's parliament was sworn in without a new government in place, after no party secured a majority the election.

item.title: NPR: Hegseth has remained defiant as Congress members deliberate articles of impeachment
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is fighting back. As members of Congress begin deliberating on the articles of impeachment against him, Hegseth gave his first press conference in months.

item.title: NPR: House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth
item.description: House Republicans managed to short circuit a floor vote on the impeachment effort brought against the Defense Secretary by Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'They want us to fight': Jeffries outlines priorities as Democrats prepare to take power
item.description: With Congress back this week, Republicans and Democrats alike are wasting no time preparing for the new session that begins in January. House Republicans elected Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan to be their next leader. Although Democrats haven't voted yet on their leadership team, Hakeem Jeffries is poised to become the speaker. He joined Amna Nawaz to outline his priorities.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Farewell to the electoral college? Democrats now control enough states to elevate the popular vote
item.description: Eighteen states run by Democrats have already joined an interstate compact to award their Electoral College votes to whichever presidential candidate wins the national popular vote.
